lines.en: F. 130r. HEADLESS EXCERPT CONCERNING PLACES 1.

lines.text: . . . μέθοδον τῆς τῶν κλήρων εὑρέσεως· φέρε οὖν ταύτην παραδώ-
lines.en: . . . method of finding the lots; come then, let us hand this down;

lines.text: σομεν· καὶ πρῶτόν γε ἀρξόμεθα ἀπὸ τοῦ κλήρου τῆς τύχης, ἐπειδὴ
lines.en: and first let us begin from the lot of fortune, since

lines.text: μᾶλλον αὕτη ἡ θεὸς συγγενεστέρα τοῖς τῇδε πέφυκεν, αὔξουσα καὶ
lines.en: this goddess is more akin to things here, increasing and

lines.text: μειοῦσα τὰ πράγματα, ὅθεν καὶ τῇ Σελήνῃ αὐτὴν ᾠκείωσεν ὁ θειότατος
lines.en: decreasing things, whence also the most divine

lines.text: 5 ἐκεῖνος Ἑρμῆς Φιβὶ ὁ Τρισμέγιστος· εἶτα μετὰ ταύτην τὸν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ
lines.en: 5 that Hermes Phibi the Trismegistus made her akin to the Moon; then after this the lot of the good

lines.text: δαίμονος, ἐπειδὴ ἤθη ψυχῆς καὶ φρόνησιν καὶ προαίρεσιν ἐκ τούτου
lines.en: daimon, since we can know the character of the soul and intelligence and choice from this,

lines.text: δυνάμεθα γινώσκειν, ὥσπερ ἐκ τῆς τύχης περὶ τοῦ σώματος καὶ τῶν
lines.en: just as from fortune concerning the body and the things

lines.text: περὶ τὸ σῶμα· περὶ ταῦτα δὲ μάλιστα ἡ μεγίστη μαντεία καταγίνεται
lines.en: concerning the body; and concerning these things especially the greatest divination is occupied

lines.text: τοῦ γνῶναι ἤθη ψυχῆς καὶ διαγωγὴν σωμάτων, ταὐτὸν δὲ εἰπεῖν πῶς
lines.en: to know the character of the soul and the conduct of bodies, to say the same thing how

lines.text: 10 μὲν ψυχὴ πολιτεύεται κατὰ τὸν τῇδε κόσμον ἄνωθεν ἐλθοῦσα, πῶς δὲ
lines.en: 10 the soul lives in this world having come from above, and how

lines.text: τὸ σῶμα καὶ τὰ περὶ τὸ σῶμα καὶ ἁπλῶς εἰπεῖν πάντα τὰ οὐκ ἐφ’ ἡμῖν
lines.en: the body and the things concerning the body and simply to say all the things not in our power

lines.text: ὑπαντήσει. τούτου χάριν πρὸ πάντων τῶν κλήρων τὸν τοῦ δαίμονος
lines.en: will meet us. For this reason before all the lots the lot of the daimon

lines.text: καὶ τῆς τύχης κλῆρον ζητητέον· ἀλλὰ μὴν καὶ ἑτέραν αἰτίαν εἶπε ὅτι
lines.en: and of fortune must be sought; but indeed he also said another reason that

lines.text: διὰ τοῦτο τὸν τοῦ δαίμονος καὶ τῆς τύχης κλῆρον δεῖ προεκβαλεῖν,
lines.en: because of this the lot of the daimon and of fortune must be cast out first,

lines.text: 15 ἐπειδὴ ἀπὸ τούτων καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους πάντας ἐκβάλλομεν· οὐκ ἠδυνάμεθα
lines.en: 15 since from these we also cast out all the others; we could not

lines.text: οὖν τούτων μὴ ἐκβληθέντων τοὺς λοιποὺς ἐκβαλεῖν. ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ταῦτα
lines.en: therefore cast out the rest if these were not cast out. Since then these things

lines.text: καλῶς εἴρηται, ἔλθωμεν ἐπὶ τὸ προκείμενον καὶ ζητήσωμεν τὴν μέθο-
lines.en: have been well said, let us come to the matter at hand and seek the method

lines.text: δον δι’ ἧς ὁ κλῆρος τῆς τύχης ἐκβάλλεται.
lines.en: by which the lot of fortune is cast out.

lines.text: Δεῖ γὰρ σκοπεῖν ἐν ποίῳ ζῳδίῳ καὶ ἐν ποίᾳ μοίρᾳ ὑπῆρχεν ὁ Ἥλιος
lines.en: For it is necessary to consider in what sign and in what degree the Sun was

lines.text: 20 κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τῆς γενέσεως ἢ ἁπλῶς εἰπεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς ἐγχειρουμένου
lines.en: 20 at the time of the birth or simply to say in every undertaking,

lines.text: πράγματος, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ ἐν ποίῳ ζῳδίῳ καὶ ποίᾳ μοίρᾳ ὑπῆρχεν ἡ
lines.en: likewise also in what sign and what degree the

lines.text: Σελήνη, πρὸς τούτοις δὲ καὶ ὁ ὡροσκόπος ἐν ποίῳ ζῳδίῳ ὑπῆρχεν καὶ
lines.en: Moon was, and in addition to these also in what sign the ascendant was and

lines.text: ἐν ποίᾳ μοίρᾳ. καὶ ὅταν ταῦτα εὑρεθῇ, εἰ μὲν ἡμερινή ἐστιν ἡ γέννησις,
lines.en: in what degree. And when these are found, if the birth is diurnal,

lines.text: τηνικαῦτα μετρεῖν τὸ ἀπὸ Ἡλίου μέχρι τῆς Σελήνης διάστημα τῶν μοι-
lines.en: then measure the distance of degrees from the Sun to the Moon;

lines.text: 25 ρῶν· εἶτα τούτῳ τῷ ἀριθμῷ τῷ εὑρεθέντι ἐν τῷ διαστήματι προσπλέ-
lines.en: 25 then to this number found in the distance add

lines.text: κειν τὸν ἀριθμὸν τὸν εὑρεθέντα ἐπὶ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου· εἶτα οὗτος ἀπο-
lines.en: the number found on the ascendant; then this is cast off

lines.text: λύειν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὡροσκόπου δίδοντα ἑκάστῳ ζῳδίῳ μοίρας λ´ καὶ
lines.en: from the ascendant giving to each sign 30 degrees and

lines.text: σκοπεῖν ἐν ποίῳ ζῳδίῳ καταλήξει ὁ ἀριθμὸς ὁ εὑρεθεὶς καὶ ἐν ποίᾳ
lines.en: consider in what sign the number found will end and in what

lines.text: μοίρᾳ καὶ ἐκεῖσε λέγειν εἶναι τὸν κλῆρον τῆς τύχης· ὑποδείγματος
lines.en: degree and there say is the lot of fortune; of an example

sections.en:
1 παραδώσωμεν ('let us hand over') the codex has. 3 τίδε ('what is this') the codex has. 4 οἰκείωσεν ('made his own') the codex has. 5 Cf. supra p. 148, 13.
Ἑρμῆν φιβὶ τὸν τρισμεγίστον (sic) ('Hermes Phibi the Trismegistus (thus)') the codex has. After ταύτην ('this') a word seems to be missing. 6 τύχης ('of fortune')
the codex has, corrected by Kroll. προέρεσιν ('choice') the codex has. 7 γινόσκειν ('to know') the codex has. 8 μαντία ('prophecy') the codex has. 9 τύχης ('of fortune') the codex has.
10 τύχη ('fortune') the codex has, corrected by Kroll. τίδε ('what is this') the codex has. 12 χάρην ('grace') the codex has. 14 προ ἐκβαλλεῖν ('before casting out') the codex has.
15 ἐκβάλωμεν ('let us cast out') the codex has. 16 ἐκβαλλεῖν ('to cast out'). 20 κατὰ ('according to')] καὶ ('and') the codex has. 21 ὑπείρχεν ('existed') the codex has. 25 τοῦτο ('this')
the codex has. 26 οὕτως ('thus') conjectured by Kroll. 28 καταλίξει ('will end') the codex has. 29 ἐκεῖσαι ('thither') the codex has.

sections.text:
1 Excerpti longioris, titulo et principio carentis, initium finemque describenda
curaveram ut auctoris nomen eruere possem. Nec spes omnino me fefellit, nam
eadem fere quae PAULUS ALEXANDRINUS in Isagoge, Witebergae a. 1588 edita,
I, 1r ss., praebet cod. Laurentianus, qui tamen interdum ab eo discrepat vel etiam
plenior est. Nec, cum Paulus illa ex Hermetis Panareto se hausisse ipse profiteatur,
satis constat utrum excerptum Laurentianum ab eodem fonte derivatum sit an,
quod verisimilius videtur, byzantinus quidam astrologus ex Paulo scholiisque ad
Paulum — fortasse Heliodori — saturam confecerit.
sections.en:
1 I had taken care to describe the beginning and end of a longer excerpt, lacking a title and a beginning,
so that I might be able to unearth the name of the author. Nor did hope entirely deceive me, for
the Laurentian codex offers almost the same things which PAULUS ALEXANDRINUS offers in the Isagoge, edited at Wittenberg in the year 1588,
I, 1r ff., which nevertheless sometimes differs from him or is even
fuller. Nor, since Paulus himself professes that he drew those things from the Panaretos of Hermes,
is it sufficiently established whether the Laurentian excerpt was derived from the same source or,
what seems more likely, a certain Byzantine astrologer composed a medley from Paulus and the scholia to
Paulus — perhaps of Heliodorus.

summary.headline: Calculating the Lot of Fortune
summary.text: An acephalous astrological excerpt explains why the Lots of Fortune and Daimon are cast first, then gives the procedure for calculating the Lot of Fortune from the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant by zodiacal signs and degrees. The apparatus identifies parallels with Paulus Alexandrinus’s Isagoge and discusses derivation from Hermes Panaretus or a Byzantine astrologer, possibly Heliodorus.
